items.q: Which of these businesses operates in the primary sector?
items.why: The primary sector extracts natural resources, such as fishing, farming and mining. Making cars is secondary and banking and retail are tertiary.

items.q: What does limited liability mean for the owners of a business?
opts: They cannot sell their shares to anyone else
They must share the profit equally
They can only lose the money they have invested
They are personally responsible for all the business's debts
items.why: With limited liability, owners can only lose what they have put into the business. Their personal belongings are safe.

items.q: A local community group objects to a factory's plan to run deliveries through the night. Which pair of stakeholders is most likely to be in conflict?
items.why: Night deliveries could increase output and profit for the owners but cause noise for local residents.

items.q: Two bakeries in different towns join together to form one business. What type of growth is this?
items.why: Joining with a business at the same stage of production in the same industry is horizontal integration.

items.q: Which of these is an example of a diseconomy of scale?
opts: The business buys raw materials in bulk at a lower price
Communication becomes slower as the business grows
The business spreads its advertising costs over more products
The business can borrow at a lower interest rate
items.why: Diseconomies of scale push up the cost per unit as a business gets too large, often because communication and coordination become harder. The other three are economies of scale.

items.q: Interest rates rise. Which business is most likely to be affected badly?
opts: A business that sells low-priced basic food
A business with a large bank loan on a variable interest rate
A business that has no debts
A business with a lot of cash in the bank
items.why: A rise in interest rates increases the repayments on a variable-rate loan, which raises costs and reduces profit.

items.q: The value of the pound falls against the euro. What is the likely effect on a UK business that sells to customers in France?
opts: Its products become cheaper for French customers
It has to pay higher tariffs
Its products become more expensive for French customers
items.why: When the pound is weaker, French customers need fewer euros to buy UK goods, so UK exports become cheaper and more competitive.

items.q: Which law sets the lowest hourly pay an employer can legally give a worker aged 21 or over?
items.why: The National Living Wage is the legal minimum hourly rate for workers aged 21 and over.

items.q: A furniture maker produces 50 oak tables, then resets its machines to make 80 pine chairs. Which production method is this?
items.why: Making a set quantity of one product before switching to another is batch production.

items.q: Which is a benefit of just-in-time stock control?
opts: The business can always meet a sudden rise in demand
Production cannot be stopped by a late delivery
Less money is tied up in stock
items.why: JIT means stock arrives only when it is needed, so less cash is tied up and less storage is needed. The other options are benefits of holding buffer stock.

items.q: What is the main difference between quality control and quality assurance?
opts: Quality control is done by every employee; quality assurance is done by inspectors
Quality control checks finished products; quality assurance checks quality at every stage
Quality assurance only happens at the end of production
Quality control is cheaper because it prevents faults
items.why: Quality control inspects products at the end. Quality assurance builds quality checks into every stage, aiming to stop faults happening in the first place.

items.q: A supermarket trains its staff to know the products well and to help customers find what they need. Which part of the sales process is this?
items.why: Knowing the products and engaging with customers are both part of good customer service during the sales process.

items.q: A manager has 12 employees who report directly to her. What is this number called?
items.why: The span of control is the number of people a manager is directly responsible for.

items.q: Which document describes the qualifications, skills and experience the ideal person for a job should have?
items.why: The person specification describes the ideal candidate. The job description describes the job itself.

items.q: Which of these is a financial method of motivating employees?
items.why: Commission is a payment linked to sales, so it is a financial method. The other three are non-financial.

items.q: Which is a benefit of on-the-job training compared with off-the-job training?
opts: Employees are away from distractions at work
It always leads to a qualification
items.why: On-the-job training happens at work, often from colleagues, so it is usually cheaper. The others describe off-the-job training.

items.q: A gym asks 200 of its members to fill in a questionnaire about opening hours. What type of market research is this?
items.why: The gym is collecting new information itself for its own purpose, so it is primary research.

items.q: A business splits its market into groups by age and income. What is this called?
items.why: Dividing a market into groups of customers with similar characteristics is market segmentation.

items.q: A new streaming service charges £1 a month for the first six months to attract customers, then raises the price. Which pricing method is this?
items.why: Starting with a low price to win customers and market share, then raising it, is penetration pricing.

items.q: Which source of finance is most suitable for a business that needs money for a few weeks to pay its suppliers?
opts: Retained profit from the next five years
items.why: An overdraft is a flexible short-term source of finance, suitable for covering a gap of a few weeks.
